findings.title: Authenticated workers can create applications against expired or unauthorised invitation links by calling the generic applications endpoint.
findings.scenario: Sara has no valid invitation to Tom's pharmacy. She obtains or guesses a numeric invite-link identifier and sends her details to the membership-applications API directly. The create endpoint only requires authentication and its serializer accepts the link ID without checking active status or expiry, bypassing the secure magic-link application route.
findings.test_needed: As unrelated authenticated Sara, POST /api/v1/membership-applications/ with a valid old or disabled invite_link integer, matching her email/DOB/role. Expect refusal and zero application creation; valid UUID magic-link flow must succeed.

owner_question.question: May Sara apply to Tom's pharmacy using the internal numeric ID of an expired or revoked invitation?
options: No, all application creation must require a valid active token
Allow only when Tom explicitly re-enables the invitation
Yes, the numeric ID is sufficient

findings.title: A pharmacy administrator can permanently delete pending and decided membership application review records through generic DELETE.
findings.scenario: Lina is authorised to review applications for Tom's pharmacy. After deciding an application, she calls DELETE on the application detail endpoint. The default ModelViewSet destroys the application and its submitted snapshot and reviewer decision, removing the employment decision audit trail instead of recording an archival state.
findings.test_needed: As scoped manager attempt DELETE on approved, rejected and pending applications; require 405/403 or audited soft-archive, preserving submitted/decision history. Verify positive review/approve/reject remains functional.

owner_question.question: Should Lina be allowed to permanently delete historic membership applications and decisions?
options: No, retain review history and permit only audited archive
Only permit irreversible deletion by an audited super-admin workflow
Yes, ordinary managers may delete application history
